item.subject: science
item.stem: In her school laboratory, Meena observes two cells under a microscope during a biology practical in Pune. Cell P is thin and flat, forming a protective lining on the inside of the cheek. Cell Q is very long with thread-like branches and carries messages between the brain and the rest of the body. Which statement best explains how the shape and structure of each cell suit its function?

options.A: Cell P is thin and flat, which helps it form a protective layer, while Cell Q is long and branched, which helps it carry messages quickly over long distances.
options.B: Cell P is long and branched so it can carry messages, while Cell Q is thin and flat so it can form a protective lining.
options.C: Both cells have the same shape because they come from the same person's body, and their shape does not affect their function.
options.D: Cell Q is long because carrying messages stretches it out over time, while Cell P is flat because it has no specific function.
